decisive_items: a vascular signal extending from the periphery into the center of the lesion
a low-echo lesion with regular, clear margins confined to the submucosal layer
submucosal mass on the lesser curvature of the stomach
response.rationale: The submucosal location, clear margins, and especially the peripheral-to-central color Doppler vascularity are characteristic of a gastric glomus tumor; GIST is more common but generally arises from the muscularis propria and lacks this distinctive Doppler pattern.

rejected.why: Leiomyoma is typically hypovascular and muscularis propria-origin, not fitting the described central Doppler vascularity.
GIST is a common differential but usually involves the fourth EUS layer and does not specifically explain the peripheral-to-central vascular flow pattern.
Gastric carcinoid is usually smaller/multiple and associated with background atrophic gastritis; the large solitary vascular submucosal mass favors glomus tumor.
